judged_text: the members endpoint applies no upper bound to the client-supplied limit param (limit = params[:limit].to_i with no max), so a request with limit=1000000 loads and serializes the entire member table. Any visitor who can see the group can request an arbitrarily large limit, forcing a full-table query and an unbounded serialized JSON payload on the request path — memory/latency exhaustion with no cap.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no maximum cap. This allows a client who can access the endpoint to request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing the server to load and serialize a very large set of group members (potentially all members of a large group) into JSON, which is a clear performance/DoS risk. The new `.json` members endpoint is explicitly used by the client (`/groups/<name>/members.json` with `limit`/`offset`).
